A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CSD-VAR paper, with all 15 pages, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A available for comparison. Text and rendered pages match except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative outputs, and a 100-participant user study in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative outputs, and user-study findings.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains identical scale-aware alternating optimization, SVD-based style rectification, and augmented K-V memories, with unchanged training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate content recontextualization and stylization using the same CSD-100 dataset and 35-image validation set. Appendix A retains the same dataset images and evaluation prompts.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DreamBooth-C, DreamBooth-S, B-LoRA, and Inspiration Tree. The textual-inversion baseline remains in the component study; UnZipLoRA remains excluded from direct comparison in Section 6.2.

E3.justification: Both retain 50 evaluation prompts with 10 generated images per prompt per concept, the same five alignment metrics, Switti/Infinity configurations, and the same 100-participant user-study design.

E4.justification: The scale-removal analysis, component ablations, and studies of K-V block placement, SVD rank, and token count are identical. Appendix A.4 also retains the same K-V memory-count ablation in Table 6.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and user-preference percentages. Neither adds repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-6 and the quantitative and qualitative figures are identical. For example, Table 1 reports CSD-VAR (Infinity) CSD-C of 0.660 and CLIP-I of 0.795 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1-12, including the scale-specific losses, SVD projection, and augmented attention, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about VAR-based content-style decomposition, the three method components, CSD-100, and superiority over the evaluated prior approaches.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of scale specialization, content leakage, and K-V tradeoffs. Section 7 preserves the limitation involving intricate subject details, and Appendix A.4 preserves the explanation for diminishing returns from additional memories.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including Adam with learning rate 0.001, 200 optimization steps, batch size 1, a single A100 GPU, 200 subconcepts, and the appendix prompts and study procedures.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements, and all 59 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 18 Jul 2025 to v2 dated 15 Mar 2026. All substantive prose, headings, and main-text and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-14 and Tables 1-6 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the sole visible difference is the version/date text recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and appendix material are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
